matched.set_a_axis: From absolute agency to agency under contestation (without communion shift)
matched.set_b_axis: From dominant agency to unchanged dominant agency
matched.overlap_description: Both sets identify the same underlying dimension (Agency–Communion) and the same essential finding: Zeus begins at an extreme Agency pole (unilateral decree from his throne, Hestia as instrument) and never crosses toward Communion. The only divergence is magnitude of change: Set A observes a slight destabilization of Zeus's confidence in unthinking compliance ('agency under contestation'), while Set B reads the position as entirely stable ('unchanged dominant agency'). Both agree no genuine internal realignment occurs.

matched.set_a_axis: From delegated trust to wary distrust
matched.set_b_axis: From subordinate instrument to suspected subordinate
matched.overlap_description: Both sets describe the same relational shift toward Hestia: an initial phase of confident, instrumental delegation (Hestia as trusted subordinate executor of Zeus's decree) giving way, after Hestia silently reinterprets the mission, to a cooler phase of displeasure, suspicion, and coercive pressure. Set A frames this in Trust–Antagonism terms; Set B frames it in Trust–Esteem with intimacy noted as low. Directionally identical: trust/esteem decline while formal subordination persists.

intrapersonal_axes.axis_name: Fixed at the Agency pole: from unilateral decree to coercive reassertion, with no movement toward communion
intrapersonal_axes.pole_start: Zeus operates from an extreme Agency pole: he summons Hestia, decrees her purpose unilaterally from his throne, defines order as obedience to his decree, and treats her as a divine instrument dispatched through a golden portal.
intrapersonal_axes.pole_end: Zeus remains Agency-dominant and low-communion: rather than moving toward cooperation or shared authority, he responds to Hestia's silent reinterpretation with intensified intimidation (chilling draft, rumbling, flickering lights, thunder, lightning, earthquake), betraying only a mild destabilization of his assumption of unthinking compliance.

trajectory.position_description: Anchored at the extreme Agency pole: Zeus commands rather than consults, issues his mission from his throne, frames order as divine prerogative, and expects his authority to be mirrored by unquestioning obedience.
key_moments: Zeus summons Hestia and decrees that she travel to the present world to restore natural order by guiding women back to hearth and home.
Zeus opens a golden portal, formally dispatching Hestia as his subordinate agent.
Zeus expects his decree to be executed without revision or reinterpretation.

trajectory.position_description: Still strongly Agency-oriented and low-communion: Zeus escalates divine pressure to enforce compliance, showing no move toward cooperation or relational warmth. Both readings converge that his position is stable; only his confidence in automatic compliance is slightly unsettled.
key_moments: Hestia discusses women's struggles with Phebe and silently redefines the hearth as shared burdens and belonging rather than forced confinement.
Zeus responds with a chilling draft, rumbling, flickering lights, thunder, lightning, and an earthquake.
Zeus appears frustrated that his authority is not being mirrored, yet he neither revises his decree nor moves toward shared authority.

intrapersonal_axes.evidence_summary: Both axis sets agree on dimension and direction: Zeus begins at an extreme Agency pole and stays there, never shifting toward Communion. Set A notes a small destabilization of his assumption of unthinking compliance ('agency under contestation'); Set B reads the position as wholly unchanged ('unchanged dominant agency'). Synthesizing, the most defensible reading is a flat arc with a minor perturbation: intensified coercion substitutes for any internal realignment. Evidence is confined to chapter 1, so confidence is medium rather than high.

relational_axes.axis_name: From delegated trust in a compliant instrument to cooling suspicion and coercive pressure
relational_axes.pole_start: Zeus relates to Hestia through confident, hierarchical trust: she is a subordinate divine instrument with medium trust and esteem, low intimacy, and an expectation that she will execute his decree faithfully and without reinterpretation.
relational_axes.pole_end: Zeus's trust in Hestia's compliance is weakened and his esteem cools; displeasure, suspicion, and antagonistic divine pressure enter the relationship even though Hestia remains formally loyal and Zeus still treats her as his agent.

trajectory.position_description: Zeus relates to Hestia through confident, hierarchical trust: he dispatches her as his instrument and expects obedience to his interpretation of order, with no indication of doubt.
key_moments: Zeus summons Hestia and decrees her mission to restore traditional order by returning women to hearth and home.
Zeus opens a golden portal, establishing Hestia's role as his subordinate agent in the present world.

trajectory.phase: Pressure and silent rebuttal / cooling suspicion
trajectory.position_description: Trust strains as Zeus registers Hestia's independent reinterpretation of the mission; he answers with coercive omens, introducing antagonism and suspicion into a relationship that remains formally hierarchical.
key_moments: Hestia silently asserts loyalty to Zeus's authority while redefining the hearth as shared burdens and belonging rather than forced confinement.
Zeus applies escalating divine pressure through a chilling draft, rumbling, flickering lights, thunder, lightning, and an earthquake.
Zeus appears displeased and suspicious rather than affirming, steering Hestia back toward his original decree.

relational_axes.evidence_summary: Both sets describe the same relational movement in the same direction: from confident instrumental delegation to cooler, more suspicious oversight. Set A emphasizes the emergence of antagonism and diminished trust; Set B emphasizes the drop in trust and esteem with intimacy remaining low. Neither set reports a rupture of loyalty or a shift in formal hierarchy—Hestia stays his agent, and Zeus substitutes intimidation for revised trust. The arc is negative (trust/esteem degrade) and rests entirely on chapter 1 evidence, warranting medium confidence.
